previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for chest pain described as pressure, concerning for acute coronary syndrome. He has a significant cardiac history including prior stents and non-STEMI. Evaluation revealed a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction with progression of coronary artery disease in the LAD, leading to percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement and balloon angioplasty. Post-procedure, he remained chest pain-free with stable vital signs. His diabetes was managed with insulin, and metformin was resumed prior to discharge. Home medications for hypertension, heart failure, hyperlipidemia, and GERD were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dual antiplatelet therapy, monitor weight, and follow up with cardiology.

 1. Diffuse three vessel coronary artery disease, especially

___ Stress echo:

represents a fair exercise tolerance for age. In response to 
stress, the ECG showed equivocal/borderline ischemic ST wave 
changes (see exercise report for details). The blood pressure 
response to stress was blunted. There was a normal heart rate

Resting images were acquired at a heart rate of 72 bpm and a

Echo images were acquired within 86 seconds after peak stress at

decrease in cavity size. There was augmentation of right 
ventricular free wall motion. 
 
IMPRESSION: fair functional exercise capacity. borderline ECG 
changes in the absence of 2D echocardiographic evidence of 
inducible ischemia to achieved workload.
